text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

Robusta futures in London closed higher following New York's sharp rise on Monday when futures ran up to near 6-week highs on speculative and trade buying amid concerns of a shortage of exchange-certified coffee for delivery against the September contract. July closed $43 higher at $1,643 per tonne. September closed $53 higher at $1,668 per tonne.

Arabica futures in New York ended mostly firmer but light local and commission house selling pared gains. October added 55 points to close at 188.90 cents/lb while December settled 1.65 cents/lb higher at 166.05 cents/lb. Prices are expected to remain fairly firm due to tight supplies of quality arabica beans and stepped up roaster demand ahead of the peak consumption season. However, traders said higher spot prices and a ballooning September/December switch could draw some coffee to the exchange and attract producer price-fixing going into the new-crop harvest.

EIU - The Economist Intelligence Unit (EIU) estimated 1998/99 exportable world coffee production to rise to 80 million 60-kg bags, up from an estimated 78.4 million bags in 1997/98 and 74.1 million bags in 1996/97. The rise in 1998/99 was mainly ascribed to a cyclical upturn in Brazil. It was added that new plantings of recent years should also boost 1998/99 Brazil output. Government efforts to increase production have already been signalled in other countries including Mexico, the EIU said. It was added that worries about the possible return of the El Nino weather pattern seem premature.

IVORY COAST - Coffee exports in June rose to 520,250 60- kg bags, up from 463,133 bags shipped the previous month. That brought total exports in the first nine months of 1996/97 (October/September) up to 2.018 million bags against 1.901 million bags by the same period in 1995/96. Exports got off to a late start in 1996/97 after low world prices in late 1996, tighter bank lending policies to exporters and quality problems slowing grading.
UNITED STATES - The CSCE reported certified coffee stocks fell by 304 60-kg bags as of July 28, to 91,774 bags. An additional 6,871 bags were pending grading, the exchange said.

BRAZIL - Brazil's government is to auction 85,800 60-kg bags of coffee from its stocks at a regular monthly auction on August 6, the Banco do Brasil said. Members of the domestic roasting and soluble coffee industry as well as exporters can participate in the auction.

MADAGASCAR ** - According to the Ministry of Finance, coffee production in 1996/97 (April/March) reached 917,000 60- kg bags, down from 1.133 million bags the previous year. The latest ICO figures for 1996/97 and 1995/96 are 706,000 and 785,000 bags respectively.
